title: Clearing the fractional inverse on a single blowup chart
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, let $J,K\subseteq R$ be ideals with $J$ finitely generated and $K\subseteq\sqrt J$, where $\sqrt J=\{x:x^a\in J\text{ for some }a\geq1\}$. Let $B_H=\operatorname{Bl}_H(\operatorname{Spec} R)$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-nagata-affine-blowup]. Suppose $f:B_K\to B_J$ is a morphism over $\operatorname{Spec}R$. For $d\geq0$ set $C_d=(K^d:J)=\{c\in R:jc\in K^d\text{ for every }j\in J\}$. For every $b\in K$ there exists an integer $e\geq1$ such that $b^e\in JC_e$ as a membership in an ideal of $R$ itself, not merely after localization. No finite generation of $K$ is assumed.

proof.text: Fix $b\in K$. The $b$-chart of $B_K$ is $\operatorname{Spec} A$, where $A=R[K/b]\subseteq R_b$ [def-nagata-affine-blowup, def-nagata-blowup-chart-ring]. Every element of $A$ has the form $c/b^d$ with $c\in K^d$, since lower-degree terms can be multiplied by missing powers of $b\in K$. Thus $KA=bA$, and $b$ is regular on $A$, including when this chart is the zero ring. Use [lem-pc-ideal-sheaf-comap-affine-extension] to identify the extended ideal of $J$ on the chart with $JA$. No finite generation of $K$ is required.

source.place: Tag 07Z3 (lemma-affine-blowup), and Tag 0804 (divisors.tex, lemma-blowing-up-affine); fraction description preceding 07Z3

proof.text: Assume an $X$-morphism $f:B_K\to B_J$ is given. The center ideal on $B_J$ is locally generated by a non-zero-divisor by [thm-nagata-blowup-principalizes-center]. Its extension along $f$ is therefore locally principal, and equals the extension of $J$ from $X$: locally both are generated by the images of the $j_t$, using [lem-pc-ideal-sheaf-comap-affine-extension]. The inclusion $K\subseteq\sqrt J$ gives $a\geq1$ with $b^a\in J$. At each stalk of this chart, if $u$ generates the extended $J$, then $b^a=uv$ for some $v$. Multiplication by $b$ remains injective after localization; hence $ux=0$ implies $b^ax=vux=0$ and then $x=0$. Thus these local generators of the ideal sheaf with affine sections $JA$ are regular. This sheaf is locally free of rank one, hence is an invertible module in the sense of [def-sc-invertible-module]. No general assertion that arbitrary pullback preserves Cartier divisors is used.

proof.text: For $d\geq0$ define the ideal $C_d=(K^d:J)=\{c\in R:jc\in K^d\text{ for every }j\in J\}$. We now obtain a positive $e_b$ with $b^{e_b}\in JC_{e_b}$ in $R$, not merely in $R_{b}$. For the chart above, choose $e\geq1$ large enough that $w_t=c_t/b^e$ with $c_t\in R$ for all $t$, and $j_uw_t=v_{ut}/b^e$ with $v_{ut}\in K^e$ for all $u,t$. Such a common $e$ exists by step 1; increasing a chart denominator from $d$ to $e$ multiplies its numerator by $b^{e-d}\in K^{e-d}$. In $R_b$ we have $j_uc_t=v_{ut}$ and $\sum_tj_tc_t=b^e$. For these finitely many equalities choose one $v\geq0$ such that multiplying every equality by $b^v$ makes it an equality in $R$; this is exactly the equivalence relation defining localization. Put $e_b=e+v$ and $c'_t=b^vc_t$. Then $j_uc'_t=b^vv_{ut}\in K^{e_b}$ for every generator $j_u$, hence $c'_t\in C_{e_b}$, and $\sum_tj_tc'_t=b^{e_b}$ in $R$.
